name: MAJORANA Demonstrator
summary: The MAJORANA Demonstrator was a low-background enriched-germanium double-beta experiment at SURF. Its low-energy data also produced published bosonic, fermionic and sterile-neutrino dark-matter searches.
detection_principle: High-purity germanium ionization provides excellent energy resolution for low-energy monoenergetic peaks and spectral shapes from absorption/scattering. Ultralow radioactivity and controlled cosmogenic activation reduce backgrounds.

sites.name: SURF
sites.location: Sanford Underground Research Facility, Lead, South Dakota
sites.site_status: Experiment site; see the phase descriptions

status.label: Completed
status.evidence: ORNL states that the enriched-detector array ended operation on 3 March 2021. Later background studies with a small natural-germanium subset and analysis of historical data do not imply continued data taking by the original array.

collaboration.participants_note: Only verified representative institutions are listed, not a complete membership roster. See the collaboration pages and author affiliations in the references.

results.summary: Upper limits on several nonstandard dark-matter interactions were released, without a discovery claim.

science_scope: This record covers experiments that directly measure possible interactions between dark matter and ordinary matter. Published exclusion limits, background events and projected sensitivities do not constitute a dark-matter discovery.
